correctness.rationale: Exact differentiation of the source CDF gives g_tau(y)=e^(-y)(y^2+k)/D. The log-density derivative equals A_tau(y)+(delta-1)g/G. The function y(g/G) extends analytically through y=0 with value 1, giving unique near-zero root y=delta-1+O((delta-1)^2) by the implicit-function theorem. For k<1, two simple positive zeros persist; for k>1 there are none beyond the origin. At k=1 a strict-concavity argument proves a pair of roots near y=1, with coefficient 2/sqrt(3(e-2)) times sqrt(delta-1). Separation on compact subsets and uniform negative tail bounds exclude extra roots. Symbolic derivatives and independent high-precision numerical examples agree. Limits and quantifiers are explicitly fixed-tau and sufficiently small exponentiation increments; finite numerical scans are not substituted for global proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2025 EHaq source supplies the CDF and plots but not the exact near-one two-maxima/one-minimum root classification or the critical O(sqrt(delta-1)) split. The 2022 baseline Haq article already reports the same threshold for its unexponentiated density; that is explicitly excluded from novelty. The main claim is the proved transition after CDF exponentiation, including the additional near-origin interior peak and rigorous exclusion of all other roots for fixed parameters near one. The 2023 power Haq article concerns a distinct transformed-variable family. Scientific priority remains vulnerable to an unindexed equivalent statement; the exact original sources and targeted comparisons were inspected.
residual_risks: A generic Lehmann-transformation modality theorem or unindexed EHaq-specific proof may cover some or all of the near-one stationary-point conclusion; no global priority claim is made.
The 2022 baseline analysis already has the same numerical tau cutoff, so novelty excludes that cutoff for the original Haq law.
The classification is asymptotic for each fixed tau and does not determine the shape for arbitrary delta>1.

value.rationale: The proposed lifetime law was motivated by density-shape flexibility; whether it has one or two interior local modes is an intrinsic model property. The theorem supplies an exact sharp cutoff in a natural nesting limit delta downward to one and quantifies the singular critical splitting. It changes interpretation of mode-based fitting and reveals an extra peak not characterized by the published qualitative discussion. Unlike a change-of-variables identity or arbitrary parameter sample, it provides an exhaustive structural local phase diagram. It is not claimed to settle global all-delta mode counts or relative mode heights.
